To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students' sense of community in an online learning environment is positively related to students' perception of the effectiveness of their instructor's directed facilitation and instructional design and organization and that (2) female online students have higher sense of community scores than their male counterparts.

the sense of community of inquiry (CoI) is a significant predictor of the sense of learning community in online environments, and that gender is a predictor of the sense that the online learning environment is an effective learning environment.

Students who perceive effective directed facilitation and instructional organization in their online learning environments report higher levels of sense of learning community than students who perceive these elements as less effective."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of community in the online learning environment.
the development of a learning community that is based upon shared purpose, connectedness, trust, and learning.
the development of an online pedagogy that is student centered, interactive, and community oriented.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
students' sense of shared purpose and connectedness in online learning environments is enhanced by the effective use of the Community of Enquiry model.
students' sense of community is enhanced by their recognition of effective facilitation and instructional design on the part of the instructor.

the sense of community in online environments is a function of the degree to which the instructor is able to facilitate and direct the learning process in a manner that is perceived to be effective and fair by the student.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
online learning communities can be created, nurtured, and sustained by instructors' directed facilitation and effective instructional design, organization and implementation.

the Community of Inquiry framework is useful in guiding online course development and that the Community of Learners is a useful construct in describing and assessing the quality of learning in online environments.
online learning environments can be designed and facilitated in such a way that students' sense of community can be increased.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Community of Inquiry framework provides a useful model for thinking about online learning environments, the role of the instructor in online learning environments, and how students experience online learning environments.
the Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework provides a useful lens for understanding the importance of the social and cognitive dimensions of the learning environment.
students who are in a learning community are more likely to report that they feel connected, that they trust their instructor and that they have a sense of shared purpose.
